text:
mia: quick heads-up — noticed a calibration shift in eval-runner when running sparse sampling + temp anneal for the new 7B-quant job. pass@k estimates drop ~6-8% vs single-sample baseline.

sam: what do you mean by "calibration shift" here? is it the predicted probabilities, or the observed pass@k?

mia: observed pass@k (empirical) is lower than before. predicted calibration curves (brier/cdf) also move; distributions look underconfident. happens only when we enable dedup-window and the new batcher that collapses identical prefixes.

alejandra: can you paste the minimal failing assertion from the runner?

mia: sure — simplified repro from the runner smoke:
```
# runner snippet (pseudo)
samples = batcher.sample(n=16, dedup_window=128, temp=0.7)
unique = dedupe(samples)
est_pass_at_k = pass_at_k_estimator(soft_scores, k=5)
assert est_pass_at_k - empirical_pass_at_k < 0.02
```
This assert flips when dedupe reduces sample diversity, est shrinks but empirical shrinks more.

thomas: is the estimator assuming samples are i.i.d.? dedupe breaks that assumption — weights need adjustment.

sam: ah yes. our pass@k unbiased estimator from the paper assumes sampling without replacement but independent draws. Dedupe = conditional sampling, so the combinatorics change. We should reweight or simulate importance weights.

alejandra: also saw BERTScore drift in the same runs — could be tokenization differences after quant step? or idf weighting mismatch between eval harness and local notebook.

mia: good catch — I compared idf files, harness was using per-dataset idf but our new onboarding pipeline accidentally pointed to global-idf-v2 (different smoothing). that changes bscore numbers by ~0.02 mean.

sam: actionable plan: (1) revert dedupe in the batchrunner for CI smoke to isolate; (2) add corrected pass@k estimator that accounts for replacement/dedupe; (3) pin idf file path in onboarding config; (4) add unit test that simulates dedupe behavior.

thomas: i can take (2) — will implement importance-weighted estimator and a small Monte Carlo check. planning to mock small combinatoric cases first.

alejandra: I'll own (3) and add a deterministic fixture for BERTScore idf so CI won't silently flip.

mia: I'll add (1) + the failing test into the runner smoke harness. quick patch idea for the estimator (pseudo):
```
# importance-weighted pass@k (sketch)
# if some samples are collapsed by dedupe, assign weight = 1 / multiplicity_estimate
weights = estimate_multiplicities(raw_samples, unique_samples)
weighted_scores = soft_scores * weights
return weighted_pass_at_k(weighted_scores, k)
```

sam: please add the Monte Carlo test to eval-tests so we can catch regressions. Also tie a tiny alert on eval-dashboard when pass@k delta > 0.05 post-quant.

eval-bot: new CI job queued: eval-smoke/dedupe-repro (will run on next push).

mia: thanks — will open two PRs: (A) runner: disable dedupe in smoke + test; (B) estimator + monte carlo test. assign thomas + alejandra for review.

thomas: estimated ETA for PR (B) EOD tomorrow.

alejandra: PR (A) and bump idf fixture incoming in a few hours.

sam: once merged, let's run the full comparing-dashboard (post-quant) to confirm both pass@k and bscore stabilize. logging suggestion: dump sample multiplicities and tokenization diffs to S3 for manual spot checks.

mia: agreed. I'll add a small CSV artifact with (sample_id, multiplicity, tokenization_hash) to the eval artifacts.

sam: word. thanks for catching this early — could've been a nasty silent regression during onboarding. :100:

mia: np — thanks team.
